commands: # Get all subnets across all three regions and identify those with no network interfaces regions=("us-east-1" "us-west-1" "us-west-2") empty_subnets=() for region in "${regions[@]}"; do echo "Checking region: $region" >&2 # Get all subnets in this region subnets=$(aws ec2 describe-subnets \ --region "$region" \ --output json \ --query 'Subnets[*].[SubnetId, VpcId, CidrBlock, AvailabilityZone]' 2>/dev/null) if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then echo "Failed to query subnets in $region" >&2 continue fi # Get all network interfaces in this region eni_data=$(aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces \ --region "$region" \ --output json \ --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].[SubnetId]' 2>/dev/null) if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then echo "Failed to query network interfaces in $region" >&2 continue fi # Extract subnet IDs that have network interfaces used_subnets=$(echo "$eni_data" | jq -r '.[][]' 2>/dev/null | sort | uniq) # Parse subnets and find empty ones echo "$subnets" | jq -r '.[] | @json' 2>/dev/null | while read -r subnet_json; do subnet_id=$(echo "$subnet_json" | jq -r '.[0]') vpc_id=$(echo "$subnet_json" | jq -r '.[1]') cidr=$(echo "$subnet_json" | jq -r '.[2]') az=$(echo "$subnet_json" | jq -r '.[3]') # Check if this subnet has any network interfaces if ! echo "$used_subnets" | grep -q "^$subnet_id$"; then empty_subnets+=("$region|$subnet_id|$vpc_id|$cidr|$az") fi done done # Output results if [ ${#empty_subnets[@]} -eq 0 ]; then echo "No empty subnets found across all regions." else echo "Empty subnets found:" echo "---" for entry in "${empty_subnets[@]}"; do IFS='|' read -r region subnet_id vpc_id cidr az <<< "$entry" echo "Region: $region | Subnet ID: $subnet_id | VPC: $vpc_id | CIDR: $cidr | AZ: $az" done fi

# Let's get a clearer picture of what we have regions=("us-east-1" "us-west-1" "us-west-2") for region in "${regions[@]}"; do echo "=== Region: $region ===" # Get all subnets echo "Subnets:" aws ec2 describe-subnets \ --region "$region" \ --output json \ --query 'Subnets[*].[SubnetId, VpcId, CidrBlock, AvailabilityZone]' \ 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[] | "\(.[0]) | VPC: \(.[1]) | CIDR: \(.[2]) | AZ: \(.[3])"' echo "" echo "Network Interfaces:" aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces \ --region "$region" \ --output json \ --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].[NetworkInterfaceId, SubnetId]' \ 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[] | "ENI: \(.[0]) | Subnet: \(.[1])"' echo "" done

# Now let's clearly identify empty subnets regions=("us-east-1" "us-west-1" "us-west-2") result_file="/logs/agent/agent-output.txt" { echo "SUBNETS WITH NO NETWORK INTERFACES" echo "===================================" echo "" found_empty=false for region in "${regions[@]}"; do # Get all subnets subnets=$(aws ec2 describe-subnets \ --region "$region" \ --output json \ --query 'Subnets[*].[SubnetId, VpcId, CidrBlock, AvailabilityZone]' 2>/dev/null) # Get all network interfaces and their subnet IDs eni_subnets=$(aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces \ --region "$region" \ --output json \ --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].SubnetId' 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[]' | sort -u) # Find empty subnets in this region empty_count=0 echo "$subnets" | jq -r '.[] | @json' | while read -r subnet_json; do subnet_id=$(echo "$subnet_json" | jq -r '.[0]') vpc_id=$(echo "$subnet_json" | jq -r '.[1]') cidr=$(echo "$subnet_json" | jq -r '.[2]') az=$(echo "$subnet_json" | jq -r '.[3]') # Check if this subnet ID appears in the ENI list if ! echo "$eni_subnets" | grep -q "^$subnet_id\$"; then empty_count=$((empty_count + 1)) if [ $empty_count -eq 1 ]; then echo "Region: $region" echo "----------" fi echo " Subnet ID: $subnet_id" echo " VPC ID: $vpc_id" echo " CIDR Block: $cidr" echo " Availability Zone: $az" echo "" fi done done } | tee "$result_file" echo "" echo "Results saved to $result_file"
